title: 1957 AHSME Problem 49
statement: The parallel sides of a trapezoid are \(3\) and \(9.\) The non-parallel sides are \(4\) and \(6.\) A line parallel to the bases divides the trapezoid into two trapezoids of equal perimeters. The ratio in which each of the non-parallel sides is divided is:

solutions.text:
Let the upper pieces of the legs of lengths \(4\) and \(6\) be \(4t\) and \(6t,\) respectively. The dividing segment appears once in each perimeter and cancels. Equal perimeters therefore give \[ \begin{aligned} 3+4t+6t &=9+4(1-t)\\ &\quad+6(1-t). \end{aligned} \] Hence \(20t=16,\) so \(t=\frac{4}{5}.\) Each leg is divided in the ratio \[ t:(1-t)=\frac45:\frac15=4:1. \]

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: A segment parallel to the bases divides both legs in the same fraction
Let the upper leg segments be \(4t\) and \(6t\); the common dividing segment cancels when the two perimeters are equated
